title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-position-watchlist-race-condition-followups's PR #385 review
description: Tracked, non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #385 (backend-position-watchlist-race-condition-followups, the same-ticker merge lost-update fix using PositionORM.version/version_id_col). These are independent of that review's one blocking finding (delete_position's new unhandled StaleDataError exposure, recorded on the parent task's own review.comments and sent back for a fix) -- none of the items below block the PR once that blocking item is addressed. Confirmed via a `code-review` skill pass run alongside the manual review, which independently corroborated two of these three items.

checklist.step: `_merge_and_commit`'s retry loop re-invokes `_merge_position` on every attempt, which re-fetches `provider.get_daily_ohlcv(existing.ticker)` (for `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge`) each time -- but that fetch's result depends only on the ticker, not on the row's current merge state, so a merge that needs several retries to win under same-ticker contention re-issues the same OHLCV provider call several times instead of once. Likely cheap in practice (CachedDataProvider's warm-cache layer should absorb repeat calls within the same request's short retry window), but it's relying on that caching layer's incidental behavior rather than `_merge_and_commit` fetching the data once itself -- worth fetching once per `_merge_and_commit` call and passing it through, or at least an explicit `decisions` entry recording why relying on the cache is an acceptable tradeoff.

The new `test_retries_exhausted_returns_503_not_an_infinite_loop` test (backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_positions.py, class TestAddPositionMergeRetryBoundsAndRequeryHardening) doesn't assert the actual number of merge attempts made before giving up -- unlike its sibling tests in TestAddPositionMergeCommitRaceHandling, which do assert exact `call_count` values. As written, it would pass identically whether `_MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS` were 1, 5, or 50, so it verifies there's SOME bound but doesn't actually pin down the retry-bound value the PR's own commentary describes testing. Add a call-count assertion (mirroring the existing `call_count["n"] == 2`/`== 3` pattern already used elsewhere in that same test module) to directly verify `_MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS` attempts are made, not more or fewer.

Migration 051c44cc730b's round-trip behavior (upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade, including the `server_default` backfill of a pre-existing row's `version` to 1) was verified only by hand during this PR's review (pr-reviewer independently reproduced it manually against a scratch DB and confirmed it's clean) -- no automated test exercises this migration's downgrade/backfill path specifically. This matches existing precedent (no other migration in this codebase has a dedicated round-trip test either -- `test_db_migrations.py`'s `TestUpgradeHeadAgainstAFreshDatabase` only checks the fresh-upgrade-to-head column set), so it's not a new gap this PR introduces below the bar, but worth considering a small, shared downgrade/backfill-round-trip test helper for migrations that add a backfilled column, applied here and retroactively to earlier similar migrations (e.g. the ones adding `entry_notes`/`strategy`/`trailing_stop_high_water_mark` to `positions`), if that pattern recurs again.

Reuse/simplification (round 2, PR #385's second commit): `_delete_position_and_commit` duplicates roughly 100 lines of retry/rollback/re-query/logging scaffolding that is nearly identical in shape to `_merge_and_commit`'s existing implementation (same bounded-attempts loop, same `(StaleDataError, IntegrityError, OperationalError)` catch, same rollback -> re-query -> row-found-vs-not branching, same per-attempt warning-log calls) -- differing only in what the per-attempt operation does (merge-and-return vs delete-and-return-None) and what happens when the row is gone on re-query (503 for merge, since there's nothing to combine with; 404 for delete, since the request's own intended outcome already happened). A shared helper parameterized by the per-attempt operation and the gone-row outcome (e.g. `_commit_with_version_retry(db, position_id, attempt_fn, max_attempts, on_row_gone)`) would remove the duplication, and would also be the natural single place to fix this same review's blocking finding (the re-query-OperationalError `continue` path leaving `row`/the loop's working state stale instead of refreshing it, risking an unhandled `ObjectDeletedError` if the row is genuinely deleted in that window) once instead of twice.

decisions.decision: Fixed checklist item 1: `_merge_and_commit` now fetches and filters this ticker's daily OHLCV (`provider.get_daily_ohlcv` + `drop_malformed_daily_bars(..., require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=False)`) exactly once, up front, before entering its retry loop, rather than once per retry attempt inside `_merge_position`. `_merge_position`'s own signature changed from `(existing, position, provider)` to `(existing, position, daily_ohlcv)` -- it now receives the already-fetched/filtered frame (or `None`) directly and no longer touches `provider`/`DataProviderError` itself at all. The single real caller of `_merge_position` outside this module (`test_portfolio_positions_lost_update_race.py`'s `_merge_position_with_barrier` monkeypatch, used to inject a synchronization barrier for a real-concurrency reproduction) was updated to match the new 3rd-parameter shape (it merely forwards whatever it receives, so this was a mechanical rename, not a behavioral change to that test).
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's own alternative (recording a decision that relying on `CachedDataProvider`'s warm-cache layer to absorb repeat calls is an acceptable tradeoff) was rejected in favor of actually fixing it: the real fetch-once behavior was straightforward to implement correctly (the OHLCV data genuinely depends only on `ticker`, fixed for the whole `_merge_and_commit` call, never on which particular row revision a given retry attempt merges against -- confirmed by reading `_merge_position`'s own pre-fix docstring, which already stated this explicitly), and fixing it outright removes a dependency on an unrelated module's incidental caching behavior rather than merely documenting reliance on it. Verified via the full existing test suite (`TestAddPositionCapturesTrailingStopFloorAtMerge`'s 5 tests, which exercise the floor-capture behavior end-to-end through real merges and a malformed-bar defense-in-depth check) passing unchanged -- none of those tests assert on `get_daily_ohlcv`'s call count, only on the resulting `trailing_stop_high_water_mark` value, so this is a pure internal-efficiency change with no behavioral difference for a single-attempt (non-retried) merge, and a strict improvement (one fetch instead of N) for a retried one.

decisions.decision: Fixed checklist item 2: added a `call_count` assertion to `test_retries_exhausted_returns_503_not_an_infinite_loop` (test_portfolio_positions.py) asserting `call_count["n"] == portfolio._MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS` exactly, mirroring the existing `call_count["n"] == 2`/`== 3` pattern already used in `TestAddPositionMergeCommitRaceHandling`. Also applied the identical fix to the delete path's own analogous test, `test_delete_retries_exhausted_returns_503_not_an_infinite_loop` (test_portfolio_delete_position.py), asserting `call_count["n"] == portfolio._MAX_POSITION_DELETE_ATTEMPTS` -- not explicitly named by this task's checklist item (which only names the merge-path test), but an identical gap of the exact same shape in the delete path's own exhausted-retries test, discovered while reading that test for the item-4 refactor below; fixing both in the same pass was a small, low-risk addition rather than leaving a known-identical gap unfixed on the other half of the same retry mechanism.
decisions.rationale: A bare '503 response with the right wording' assertion (the pre-fix state) would pass identically whether the configured retry bound were 1, 5, or 50 -- it verifies a bound exists but not which one, exactly the gap the checklist item describes. Mutation-tested directly: temporarily changed the merge path's `_commit_with_version_retry` call site to pass a hardcoded `max_attempts=3` (desynced from the real `_MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS = 5` the test reads), re-ran the now-fixed test, and confirmed it failed (`assert 3 == 5`) -- proving the new assertion actually pins down the configured bound rather than just checking 'some bound was enforced'. Restored afterward and reconfirmed the full suite green.

decisions.decision: Left checklist item 3 (no automated round-trip test for migration 051c44cc730b's upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade/backfill behavior) as a documented non-issue rather than adding a new test for it in this task.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's own text already concludes this 'is not a new gap this PR introduces below the bar' -- it matches existing codebase-wide precedent (no other migration, including the `entry_notes`/`strategy`/`trailing_stop_high_water_mark` migrations it names as comparable, has a dedicated round-trip test either), and pr-reviewer and pr-decision both already independently hand-verified the specific round-trip behavior against a scratch SQLite DB as part of PR #385's own review (recorded on that task's `review`/`pr_decision` entries) rather than leaving it unverified. Introducing a one-off round-trip test for just this migration, with no shared helper and no retroactive application to the other similarly-shaped migrations the item itself suggests, would create an inconsistent, singular exception to an established codebase-wide pattern rather than a genuine improvement -- the item's own suggested shape (a *shared* downgrade/backfill-round-trip helper applied consistently) is a reasonable idea but is itself a new, nontrivial piece of shared test infrastructure scoped well beyond this followups task's narrow review-finding remit, and better suited to its own dedicated task if the pattern recurs again, as the checklist item itself frames it ('if that pattern recurs again'). No code or test change was made for this item; it's closed by this decision.

decisions.decision: Fixed checklist item 4: extracted the shared `_commit_with_version_retry[T]` helper (app/api/routers/portfolio.py) and rebuilt both `_merge_and_commit` and `_delete_position_and_commit` on top of it, removing the ~100-line duplicated retry/rollback/re-query/logging scaffolding between them. The helper takes the current `row`, a per-attempt `attempt_fn(row) -> T` (merge-and-return-the-row for the merge caller; the `ClosedTradeORM`-insert-plus-`db.delete` for the delete caller, returning `None`), a `requery_fn() -> PositionORM | None`, and two outcome callbacks -- `on_row_gone(attempt, last_exc) -> NoReturn` and `on_exhausted(last_exc) -> NoReturn` -- that each call site implements with its own status code/detail/log wording (503-transient vs 404 for row-gone; both 503 but differently worded for exhausted-retries), since those two outcomes are the one place a merge and a delete genuinely need different behavior, not just different wording. The helper itself owns the one retryable mechanism shared identically by both: the bounded attempt loop, the `(StaleDataError, IntegrityError, OperationalError, ObjectDeletedError)` catch, the inner re-query-`OperationalError`-folds-into-the-same-retry handling (the exact mechanism PR #385's own checklist item 2 and round-2 review both centered on), and the row-found-vs-not branching. Used Python's PEP 695 generic-function syntax (`def _commit_with_version_retry[T](...)`) matching existing precedent in this codebase (`app/api/day_trader_signal.py`'s `_fan_out_per_ticker[T]`, `app/api/routers/stocks.py`'s `_fetch_via_scoped_provider[T]`) rather than an explicit `TypeVar`.
decisions.rationale: This was deferred twice before (PR #385's round-2 `decisions` entry explicitly reasoned that bundling a structural extraction into an already-multi-round blocking-fix pass would raise the risk of introducing a third subtle bug under the same time pressure that produced the first two) -- but PR #385 is now fully merged and stable (confirmed via `git log`: 9a3447f7), so that specific risk (compounding an extraction with an in-flight urgent bug fix) no longer applies; this task gets its own focused review instead, exactly as that prior entry anticipated. The extraction was verified with the mutation-testing rigor this exact area's 3-round review history (PR #385 rounds 1-3, each finding a genuine subtle concurrency bug) demands, specifically targeting the mechanisms the extraction touches: (1) temporarily removed `ObjectDeletedError` from the shared except tuple -- both `test_requery_operational_error_then_row_genuinely_deleted_raises_handled_503` and its delete-path analog `..._404` failed with the exact raw unhandled `ObjectDeletedError` traceback described by PR #385's own round-2 finding; (2) temporarily replaced the inner requery-`OperationalError` handler's `continue` with a no-op -- both `test_requery_operational_error_is_retried_not_unhandled` tests (merge and delete) failed with `UnboundLocalError` (confirming that branch's fall-through behavior is genuinely load-bearing and exercised, not dead code); (3) temporarily swapped the row-gone branch to call `on_exhausted` instead of `on_row_gone` -- four tests across both call sites failed on the wrong status code (503 instead of 404, or vice versa), confirming the helper correctly routes each call site to its own distinct outcome callback rather than conflating them; (4) temporarily desynced the merge path's own `max_attempts` from `_MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS` (see the item-2 decision above) -- caught by the newly-added call-count assertion. One mutation (removing the `row = refreshed` reassignment after a successful re-query) did NOT cause any test to fail -- traced this to SQLAlchemy's session identity map: `requery_fn()` returns the same already-identity-mapped Python object `row` already referenced (since every re-query in this codebase's actual usage runs against the SAME session the original `row`/`existing` came from), and `db.rollback()` already expires that object's attributes regardless, so the next attribute access lazy-reloads fresh data from the DB whether or not the local `row` variable is explicitly reassigned to the re-query's return value. This reassignment is kept (not removed) despite being incidentally redundant under this codebase's current single-session usage: removing it would be a correctness-adjacent change outside this task's narrow deduplication scope, and the explicit reassignment keeps the code's own stated intent (operate on the freshly-queried instance) correct and self-evident even if SQLAlchemy's identity-map behavior, this codebase's session-sharing pattern, or a future caller passing an independent session ever changed. After each mutation, restored the fix and reconfirmed the full backend suite green with zero residual diff. Final state: full suite 1613 passed, 100% line/branch coverage (gate 90%); ruff and mypy both clean; `python scripts/export_openapi.py` reproduces `backend/openapi.json` byte-for-byte (purely internal refactor, no API-contract-visible change, consistent with this being internal error-handling restructuring only); `scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py` clean.

comments.summary: Full backend suite: 1613 passed, 100% line/branch coverage (gate 90%) -- matches the PR's claim. ruff, mypy, and scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py all clean. backend/openapi.json re-exported and byte-identical -- correctly unchanged for a pure internal refactor with no route/schema change.

Re-ran every named PR #382/#385 regression test by exact nodeid against the refactored code (not just the aggregate suite count): the real two-OS-thread concurrency tests (test_two_real_concurrent_requests_for_the_same_existing_ticker_lose_no_update, test_delete_survives_a_concurrent_merge_update_of_the_same_position), the StaleDataError lost-update tests, both ObjectDeletedError-on-re-query-failure tests (merge path's test_requery_operational_error_then_row_genuinely_deleted_raises_handled_503 and delete path's ..._404), the concurrent-insert-race tests, and both new exact-call-count retries-exhausted tests -- all genuinely pass against the extracted _commit_with_version_retry helper.

Independently reproduced (not just trusted the worker's self-report) two of the claimed mutations by editing the checked-out file directly and reverting after each: (1) removing ObjectDeletedError from the shared except tuple in _commit_with_version_retry -- both affected regression tests failed with the exact raw unhandled traceback described by PR #385's round-2 finding; (2) desyncing the merge call site's max_attempts from _MAX_POSITION_MERGE_ATTEMPTS -- caught by the new exact-call-count assertion. Also independently reproduced a third mutation beyond what was asked (swapping on_row_gone for on_exhausted in the row-gone branch) -- 4 tests failed on the wrong status code (503 vs 404), confirming the two outcome callbacks are supplied per-call-site as explicit closures (not selected via any shared/global dispatch), so they structurally cannot cross between the merge and delete callers.

Grepped every caller of _merge_position after its signature change (provider -> daily_ohlcv): exactly one production call site (the lambda inside _merge_and_commit) and one test monkeypatch wrapper (test_portfolio_positions_lost_update_race.py's _merge_position_with_barrier), both already updated to the new 3-arg shape. No stale caller found.

Traced the OHLCV-fetch-once-vs-retry-staleness question through trailing_stop_floor_before_merge's own docstring and implementation: daily_ohlcv's only consumer in the merge path is this one-way MAX-ratchet floor computation, which is explicitly documented as tolerant of staleness (can only ever under-advance the floor, never let it regress, and catches up on a later successful merge). Fetching once up front rather than per-retry-attempt doesn't introduce a new correctness risk: the retry window is bounded by local SQLite lock-contention resolution (milliseconds), far too short for a materially newer daily bar to appear, and the function's own degrade-gracefully contract already absorbs the case where it did. Not a bug.

Non-blocking: independently investigated the 'row = refreshed is incidentally redundant' claim beyond reproducing the no-test-fails mutation. Constructed a scenario the existing suite doesn't cover -- a concurrent delete-and-reinsert of the SAME ticker under a DIFFERENT primary key during one merge's retry window (not just an in-place update/delete of the same row) -- and found that with the line removed, this specific scenario causes the merge to spuriously exhaust all retries and 503 even though a valid, mergeable row exists throughout (the stale/deleted row reference keeps raising ObjectDeletedError, and the fresh re-query result is discarded every time since the local `row` variable is never reassigned). With the line present (the shipped code), the same scenario correctly completes the merge. The decision to keep the line is correct, but its recorded rationale ('incidentally redundant... kept for correctness-intent clarity') understates the real risk -- it's load-bearing for this reachable (if rare) race, not just a stylistic safeguard. Tracked as a follow-up task (backend-position-watchlist-race-condition-followups-followups-followups) to correct the decisions-entry text and add a regression test for this exact scenario.

Backend-only diff (area backend/portfolio); no app/signals/ or app/portfolio/risk.py changes, confirmed via diff stat -- no Elder Triple Screen/Impulse/confidence/2%-6%-rule methodology logic touched. The one methodology-adjacent call (trailing_stop_floor_before_merge) is invoked with identical arguments/semantics, just relocated for the fetch-once optimization; TestAddPositionCapturesTrailingStopFloorAtMerge's 5 tests confirm unchanged behavior. No divergence from docs/Analyse.md. No new module/dependency/layer added (one new private helper function in the existing router file), so architecture-review wasn't separately warranted.

Browser/UI-facing check: no live Playwright MCP browser tool was available in this review session, so the exploratory walkthrough (step 9) was done via direct HTTP calls against the running dev backend instead, exercising the exact changed code paths a UI click would hit -- golden-path add, duplicate-ticker merge (hits _merge_and_commit), delete (hits _delete_position_and_commit), and delete-of-missing-id (404 edge case) -- all behaved correctly with no server errors. The persisted e2e suite (step 9a, make e2e) WAS run with a real headless browser and passed all 27 specs, including portfolio.spec.ts's add/view/close-position flows end to end.

review.notes: Especially thorough re-review per the dispatch instructions, given this touches the same concurrency-critical retry/commit code that took 3 review rounds on PR #385 to get right. All four summarized changes (fetch-OHLCV-once, exact-call-count retry-bound tests, the migration-round-trip documented-non-issue, and the _commit_with_version_retry[T] extraction) verified independently rather than taking the PR description's self-reported verification at face value: full suite + coverage re-run, static analysis re-run, every named PR #382/#385 regression test re-run by exact nodeid, 3 mutations independently reproduced (2 requested + 1 extra), the signature-change caller grep done directly, the staleness question traced through the actual consumer function, and a brand-new scenario constructed and run against both the shipped code and a local mutation to pressure-test the 'row = refreshed is redundant' claim specifically. One non-blocking finding from that last investigation, tracked as a follow-up task. No blocking findings: tests/coverage/lint/types/OpenAPI snapshot/decision-memory/methodology conformance all pass.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran the full backend suite (1613 passed, 100% line/branch coverage) plus ruff/mypy/check_profit_target_wording.py, all clean, matching pr-reviewer's claims. Re-ran all 11 named PR #382/#385/#387 regression tests by exact nodeid (both real two-OS-thread concurrency tests, both ObjectDeletedError-on-requery tests, the StaleDataError lost-update test, both exact-call-count retries-exhausted tests, etc.) against the refactored _commit_with_version_retry helper -- all pass. Reproduced the ObjectDeletedError mutation myself (removed it from the shared except tuple; both affected tests failed with the exact raw unhandled traceback, then restored with zero residual diff). Independently wrote and ran my own reproduction of the reviewer's delete-and-reinsert-with-new-PK scenario (not just read the code): with the shipped `row = refreshed` reassignment present, the simulated race correctly completes the merge (201); with it removed, the merge spuriously exhausts all retries and 503s despite a valid mergeable row existing throughout -- confirming the follow-up task's finding is correct and the line is genuinely load-bearing. Skimmed the full diff (portfolio.py + 3 test files + task-board bookkeeping); the extraction matches its documented shape and the non-blocking follow-up (backend-position-watchlist-race-condition-followups-followups-followups) and its parent index.json entries are correctly filed.
